hits.name: neuroblastoma
hits.description: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most common solid, extracranial childhood tumor. It is an aggressive pediatric cancer that originates from neural crest tissues of the sympathetic nervous system.

hits.name: Adrenal Gland Neuroblastoma
hits.description: A neuroblastoma arising from the adrenal gland.

hits.name: retroperitoneal neuroblastoma
hits.description: A neuroblastoma that involves the retroperitoneal space.

hits.name: neuroblastoma, susceptibility to, 3
hits.description: Any neuroblastoma in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the ALK gene.

hits.name: Mediastinal Neuroblastoma
hits.description: A neuroblastoma arising from the mediastinum.

hits.name: Olfactory Neuroblastoma
hits.description: An olfactory neuroblastoma arising in the paranasal sinus.

hits.name: extracranial neuroblastoma
hits.description: A neuroblastoma arising from an anatomic site other than the brain.

hits.name: cerebral neuroblastoma
hits.description: A neuroblastoma arising from the cerebral hemispheres.

hits.name: retinal neuroblastoma
hits.description: A neuroblastoma arising from the retina.

hits.name: dopaminergic neuroblastoma
hits.description: A neuroblastoma associated with increased dopamine excretion.

hits.name: Hirschsprung disease-ganglioneuroblastoma syndrome
hits.description: A rare, genetic, developmental defect during embryogenesis syndrome characterized by total or partial colonic aganglionosis associated with peripheral, usually multifocal, neuroblastic tumors (ganglioneuroblastoma, neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroma). Congenital central hypoventilation syndrome, with variable severity of respiratory compromise, cardiovascular and ophthalmologic symptoms, consistent with autonomic nervous system dysfunction, is occasionally associated.

hits.name: skin neoplasm
hits.description: Tumors or cancer of the SKIN.

hits.name: mediastinal neural neoplasm
hits.description: A neurogenic tumor that arises from the mediastinum. Neural tumors are the most common tumors that arise from the posterior mediastinum. Representative examples include Schwannoma, neurofibroma, and neuroblastoma.

hits.name: immune system disease
hits.description: A group of non-neoplastic and neoplastic disorders resulting from the deregulation and/or deficiency of immune system functions.  It includes autoimmune disorders (e.g., lupus erythematosus, dermatomyositis, rheumatoid arthritis), congenital and acquired immunodeficiency syndromes including the acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS), and neoplasms (e.g., lymphomas and malignancies secondary to transplantation.)

hits.name: skin disease
hits.description: Any deviation from the normal structure or function of the skin or subcutaneous tissue that is manifested by a characteristic set of symptoms and signs.

hits.name: thyroid neoplasm
hits.description: A benign or malignant neoplasm affecting the thyroid gland.

hits.name: thyroid cancer
hits.description: A malignant neoplasm involving the thyroid gland

hits.name: benign neoplasm
hits.description: A neoplasm which is characterized by the absence of morphologic features associated with malignancy (severe cytologic atypia, tumor cell necrosis, and high mitotic rate). Benign neoplasms remain confined to the original site of growth and do not metastasize to other anatomic sites.

hits.name: thyroid carcinoma
hits.description: A carcinoma arising from the thyroid gland. It is usually an adenocarcinoma and includes the following main subtypes: follicular, papillary, medullary, poorly differentiated, and anaplastic.

hits.name: BARD1-related cancer predisposition
hits.description: Hereditary cancer predisposition due to variation(s) in the BARD1 gene. Germline pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in the BARD1 gene confer a moderate risk of breast cancer, inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern, increasingly documented to be specific to triple negative breast cancer in women. BARD1 cancer susceptibility syndrome is also associated with other tumour types including neuroblastoma.

hits.name: lymphatic malformation
hits.description: Primary lymphedema is caused by anatomic or functional defects in the lymphatic system, resulting in chronic swelling of body parts and lymphatic-system malformation.

hits.name: lymphedema
hits.description: Excess fluid collection in tissues, causing swelling. It is the result of obstruction of lymphatic vessels or lymph nodes.
